title: Large language model uncertainty proxies: discrimination and calibration for medical diagnosis and treatment
authors: Thomas Savage, John Wang, Robert Gallo, Abdessalem Boukil, Vishwesh Patel, Seyed Amir Ahmad Safavi-Naini, Ali Soroush, Jonathan H. Chen
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association 32(1):139-149 (online 2024-10-12)
objective: Assess whether uncertainty proxies quantify LLM confidence for diagnosis and treatment selection
architecture_methods: Compared confidence elicitation (verbalized), token-level probability, sample consistency (sentence-embedding and GPT-annotation variants)
dataset_sample: 3 datasets of open-ended patient scenarios (diagnosis and treatment)
main_findings: SC with sentence embeddings ROC AUC 0.68-0.79 but poorly calibrated; SC with GPT annotation ROC AUC 0.66-0.74 with accurate calibration; verbalized confidence consistently overestimated confidence; SC most effective proxy tested
limitations: Abstract only read; no abstention/coverage metrics reported in abstract
relevance: P2/RQ1: basis for not using self-reported confidence to trigger ABSTAIN
supports_or_contradicts: Supports external/consistency-based abstention triggers; neutral on multi-agent
claims_supported: Verbalized LLM confidence is overconfident in medical diagnosis/treatment; sample consistency is the best tested proxy but only moderately discriminative

title: Large Language Models lack essential metacognition for reliable medical reasoning
authors: Maxime Griot, Coralie Hemptinne, Jean Vanderdonckt, Demet Yuksel
objective: Evaluate metacognitive abilities of LLMs in medical reasoning
architecture_methods: MetaMedQA: MCQ with confidence scores and metacognitive tasks (missing correct answer, unknown questions)
metrics: Confidence-based accuracy, missing-answer recall, unknown recall
main_findings: All models showed significant metacognitive deficits despite high MCQ accuracy; often gave confident answers when the correct option was missing (per-model numbers not read)
limitations: Full text not accessed; MCQ format
relevance: P2/RQ1: LLMs fail to recognise unanswerable cases
supports_or_contradicts: Supports need for explicit ABSTAIN/NEED_MORE_INFO mechanisms
claims_supported: LLMs rarely recognise knowledge limits or missing answers in medical QA

title: Knowing When to Abstain: Medical LLMs Under Clinical Uncertainty
authors: Sravanthi Machcha, Sushrita Yerra, Sahil Gupta, Aishwarya Sahoo, Sharmin Sultana, Hong Yu, Zonghai Yao
published_version_checked: no - an ACL Anthology entry 2026.eacl-long.291 appeared in search but was not opened; unconfirmed
objective: Benchmark abstention of medical LLMs under clinical uncertainty (MedAbstain)
architecture_methods: Conformal prediction (LAC, APS; alpha=0.1; 30/70 calibration/test), perturbations removing key details, explicit abstention option; settings NA, A, NAP, AP; zero/few-shot, CoT, thinking mode
models_tools: Open and closed LLMs incl. GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini, Qwen (thinking on/off)
metrics: Accuracy, conformal set size, abstention rate, human-judged abstention precision/recall
main_findings: Humans judged 77.55% of perturbed cases as warranting abstention; model abstention precision 71.43%, recall 13.16% on AP subset; few-shot/CoT negligible gains in abstention; Qwen thinking mode slightly improved accuracy but reduced abstention rate
limitations: MCQ only; English only; closed-model logprob artefacts; per-model accuracies not extracted
relevance: P2/RQ1: provides precision/recall template for over- vs under-abstention
supports_or_contradicts: Supports need for abstention mechanisms; suggests under-abstention, not over-abstention, dominates in MCQ
claims_supported: Medical LLMs rarely abstain when warranted even with an explicit option

title: MediQ: Question-Asking LLMs and a Benchmark for Reliable Interactive Clinical Reasoning
authors: Shuyue Stella Li, Vidhisha Balachandran, Shangbin Feng, Jonathan S. Ilgen, Emma Pierson, Pang Wei Koh, Yulia Tsvetkov
published_version_checked: yes - NeurIPS 2024 virtual poster page (track not explicitly stated)
objective: Evaluate and improve LLMs that ask follow-up questions instead of answering under incomplete information
architecture_methods: Patient system + Expert system; abstention modules: numerical, binary, scale, rationale generation, self-consistency; thresholds by grid search on dev
main_findings: GPT-4 iMEDQA Full 79.7% vs Initial 54.5%; BASIC 55.4%; best (Scale+RG+SC) 66.1%. GPT-4 iCRAFT-MD Full 91.4, Initial 67.9, BASIC 73.6, best 84.3. Best system +22.3% over BASIC (relative/absolute unclear). Self-consistency alone degraded performance. Accuracy stagnates with irrelevant/repetitive questions
limitations: Simulated patients; MCQ-derived; best still below full-information upper bound
relevance: P2/RQ1: NEED_MORE_INFO behaviour; P1 information gathering
supports_or_contradicts: Supports confidence-gated asking; shows naive asking and SC alone can hurt
claims_supported: Withholding information sharply lowers LLM accuracy; abstention-gated question asking partially recovers it

title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
authors: Bingbing Wen, Jihan Yao, Shangbin Feng, Chenjun Xu, Yulia Tsvetkov, Bill Howe, Lucy Lu Wang
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics 13:529-556
metadata_verified_via: ACL Anthology (verified 2026-11-23 in earlier pass; page blocked this pass)
objective: Survey abstention methods, benchmarks and metrics in LLMs
architecture_methods: Framework: query, model, human-values perspectives
main_findings: Frames abstention as safety/hallucination mitigation; identifies abstention as an open meta-capability
limitations: Survey; metrics section not read
supports_or_contradicts: Supports abstention as an open research problem
claims_supported: Abstention is an established, open research area

title: Enhancing the reliability and accuracy of AI-enabled diagnosis via complementarity-driven deferral to clinicians
authors: K. Dvijotham, J. Winkens, M. Barsbey, et al.
objective: Learn when to defer from a predictive AI model to the clinical workflow
architecture_methods: CoDoC learned deferral between AI opinion and clinical workflow
models_tools: Commercial and research imaging AI systems (non-LLM)
dataset_sample: Mammography (UK OPTIMAM, US datasets); TB chest X-ray (Stop TB Partnership, icddr,b); sizes not read
metrics: False positives at fixed false-negative rate; clinician workload
baselines: Double reading with arbitration; standalone AI; clinical workflow
main_findings: UK breast screening: 25% fewer false positives at same false-negative rate and 66% less clinician workload vs double reading; TB: 5-15% fewer false positives for 3 of 5 AI systems
limitations: Not LLM; imaging only; abstract only
relevance: P2/RQ1: deferral evaluated at fixed error rate; template for escalation metrics
supports_or_contradicts: Supports learned/explicit deferral as safety mechanism
claims_supported: Deferral to clinicians can improve both safety and efficiency when evaluated at a fixed error rate

title: AgentMD: Empowering language agents for risk prediction with large-scale clinical tool learning
authors: Qiao Jin, Zhizheng Wang, Yifan Yang, Qingqing Zhu, Donald Wright, Thomas Huang, Nikhil Khandekar, Nicholas Wan, Xuguang Ai, W. John Wilbur, Zhe He, R. Andrew Taylor, Qingyu Chen, Zhiyong Lu
objective: Language agent that curates and applies clinical calculators
architecture_methods: Tool builder (2,164 executable calculators from PubMed) + tool user (selects and executes calculators)
dataset_sample: RiskQA-type evaluation (size not read); 698 real ED notes
main_findings: 87.7% vs 40.9% accuracy for GPT-4; calculators >85% quality-check accuracy, >90% unit-test pass
limitations: Abstract only
relevance: Hybrid deterministic tools; RQ4 tool-matched baseline needed
supports_or_contradicts: Supports deterministic computation over LLM reasoning for computable logic
claims_supported: Executable calculators as LLM tools greatly outperform pure LLM risk estimation

title: Large language model agents can use tools to perform clinical calculations
authors: Alex J. Goodell, Simon N. Chu, Dara Rouholiman, Larry F. Chu
objective: Test whether tool augmentation fixes LLM clinical calculation errors
architecture_methods: RAG, code interpreter, task-specific calculators (OpenMedCalc)
main_findings: Unaided ChatGPT wrong in one-third of trials (n=212); task-specific tools reduced errors from 88% to 16% (LLaMa) and 64% to 4.8% (GPT)
limitations: Abstract only; RAG/code-interpreter arms not reported in abstract
supports_or_contradicts: Supports deterministic tools
claims_supported: LLMs cannot reliably calculate; deterministic calculators cut errors several-fold

title: CDR-Agent: Intelligent Selection and Execution of Clinical Decision Rules Using Large Language Model Agents
authors: Zhen Xiang, Aliyah R. Hsu, Austin V. Zane, Aaron E. Kornblith, Margaret J. Lin-Martore, Jasmanpreet C. Kaur, Vasuda M. Dokiparthi, Bo Li, Bin Yu
objective: Select and deterministically execute clinical decision rules from notes
architecture_methods: Embedding-based CDR selection with anomaly test; GPT-4o variable extraction; deterministic Python CDR execution; missing variables imputed as negative
dataset_sample: 400 synthetic PECARN notes; CDR-Bench 144 real notes (MIMIC-IV, MedQA, ACN); 15 trauma CDRs
metrics: Exact-match selection accuracy, F1, sensitivity, specificity, time
baselines: Standalone GPT-4o with all CDR text
main_findings: Synthetic: EA 0.983 vs 0.420, F1 0.994 vs 0.735. CDR-Bench: EA 0.513 vs 0.426; F1 0.592 vs 0.608 (baseline higher); sensitivity 0.683 vs 0.936 (baseline higher); specificity 0.983 vs 0.652
limitations: Proxy imaging labels inferred by GPT-4o; negative imputation; trauma only; text/table inconsistencies
relevance: Hybrid rule execution; P2 missing-value handling; RQ4
supports_or_contradicts: Supports hybrid on synthetic data; mixed on real notes (loss of sensitivity)
claims_supported: Deterministic CDR execution improves selection accuracy but defaulting missing variables to negative reduces sensitivity

title: More Reasoning Is Not Always Better: Executing Clinical Guidelines with LLMs and Rules
authors: Xiaoqian Lu, Guangfu Guo, Long Cheng, Kunpeng Liu
objective: Compare LLM-executed vs rule-executed guideline decision making
architecture_methods: MedDEx: LLM extraction -> deterministic rule executor over guideline decision graph (derived values e.g. TNM) -> LLM answer restricted to executor options
dataset_sample: MedGUIDE 7,747 MCQs/53 trees; MEGA-CDP 7,458 cases/440 guidelines; LungCURE 1,000 lung cancer cases
metrics: Option accuracy, conclusion agreement, path similarity, TNM accuracy, plan F1, calls/latency/tokens
baselines: Single LLM, Guideline-RAG, MedAgents, MDAgents, MA-RAG, DermAgent, LCAgent
main_findings: MEGA-CDP conclusion (Qwen3-8B) 96.29 vs 83.17 single LLM; MedGUIDE 69.70 vs 68.77; scenario routing executor 79.9% vs best prompting 59.5%; MedAgents 56.09 and MDAgents 50.29 below single LLM 66.65 (Llama MedGUIDE); 2.0 vs 20.7 calls per case vs MedAgents
limitations: Small models; author-validated rule packs; best TNM accuracy 30.30%; benchmark agreement not clinical reliability
relevance: Closest analogue to proposed decision core; P4/RQ4 compute and baselines
supports_or_contradicts: Supports deterministic execution; contradicts multi-agent premise (multi-agent below single LLM); prior art against novelty claim
claims_supported: Deterministic guideline execution beats LLM-executed reasoning on routing; multi-agent baselines can underperform single LLM at ~10x calls

title: Enhancing Large Language Models for Clinical Decision Support by Incorporating Clinical Practice Guidelines
authors: David Oniani, Xizhi Wu, Shyam Visweswaran, Sumit Kapoor, Shravan Kooragayalu, Katelyn Polanska, Yanshan Wang
published_version_checked: no - ICHI 2024 cited by Xu et al. CEUR 2025; IEEE record not opened
objective: Inject a clinical guideline into LLM decision making
architecture_methods: Binary Decision Tree traversal, Program-Aided Graph Construction, CoT few-shot
dataset_sample: 39 synthetic patients; COVID-19 outpatient treatment guideline (CDC/IDSA)
metrics: F-score; physician human evaluation (incorrect, omission, harmful)
main_findings: GPT-4 BDT F 1.001 (unexplained >1), CoT-FSP 0.972, PAGC 0.834 vs zero-shot 0.47; PaLM 2 BDT 0.715 vs 0.01; best automatic method ranked lowest in human evaluation
limitations: Synthetic; one guideline; two author-physician raters; scale direction unconfirmed
supports_or_contradicts: Supports guideline structuring; automatic vs human evaluation conflict
claims_supported: Structured guideline encodings improve LLM guideline adherence over zero-shot

title: Using Clinical Guidelines, Domain Ontology, and LLMs for Personalized Leukemia Treatment Recommendations
authors: Xingru Xu, Michel Dumontier, Chang Sun
venue: SeWebMeDa-2025 workshop, CEUR Workshop Proceedings Vol-4001
objective: Compare ways to give LLMs guideline knowledge for ALL treatment
architecture_methods: Baseline, RAG, markdown+CoT, guideline graph linked to HPO/Orphanet
main_findings: Monotonic gains baseline<RAG<CoT<graph; GPT-4 graph 0.662-0.698
limitations: Synthetic, preliminary, not clinically validated
supports_or_contradicts: Supports structured knowledge injection (weak evidence)
claims_supported: Ontology-linked guideline graphs outperform plain RAG in a small synthetic study

title: Large language models and conditional rules in clinical decision support systems
authors: Shangeetha Sivasothy, Adrian Bingham, Irini Logothetis, Scott Barnett, Mohamed Abdelrazek, Carl Luckhoff, Joseph Mathew, Rajesh Vasa, Kon Mouzakis
objective: Test whether LLMs/LRMs can generate a CDSS triage rule set
architecture_methods: Prompted rule generation compared with PiMS COVID-19 triage rules
models_tools: GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o, Gemini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet; o1-mini, Grok-4, Claude 4 Sonnet
main_findings: Without PiMS variables LLMs produced screening not triage rules; with variables LLM accuracy 31.62%-70.71%, LRMs up to 81.70%
limitations: Abstract only; single COVID triage tool
supports_or_contradicts: Contradicts relying on LLM-generated rules; supports clinician/guideline-authored packs
claims_supported: LLMs are limited at reproducing clinical rule sets

title: Leveraging Medical Knowledge Graphs Into Large Language Models for Diagnosis Prediction: Design and Application Study
authors: Yanjun Gao, Ruizhe Li, Emma Croxford, John Caskey, Brian W Patterson, Matthew Churpek, Timothy Miller, Dmitriy Dligach, Majid Afshar
objective: Inject UMLS knowledge-graph paths into LLM diagnosis generation
architecture_methods: DR.KNOWS: UMLS/SNOMED KG, graph path ranking with attention, paths added to prompts
main_findings: ChatGPT 5-shot CUI-F 20.96->26.02, ROUGE-L 21.23->25.43 with paths; zero-shot ROUGE-L fell 19.77->15.49; human eval omission 16% vs 10% (P=.16, ns)
limitations: Concept extractor limits; irrelevant/contradictory paths; small human eval
supports_or_contradicts: Mixed support for KG injection
claims_supported: KG path injection gives modest, inconsistent gains and LLMs may ignore correct paths

title: Neuro-symbolic AI for auditable cognitive information extraction from medical reports
authors: George A. Prenosil, Thilo K. Weitzel, Sandra C. Bello, Clemens Mingels, Giulia Manzini, Lorenz P. Meier, Kuang-Yu Shi, Axel Rominger, Ali Afshar-Oromieh
objective: Auditable extraction by combining LLM with rule-based expert system
architecture_methods: GPT-4 fact extraction checked by Prolog expert system (Plato-3) via RUDS platform; PII blocking
main_findings: Study inclusion F1 0.63 (GPT-4) vs 1.00 (neuro-symbolic) vs 1.00 (physicians); recurrence F1 0.95 vs 1.00 vs 0.99; GPT-4 inclusion sensitivity 0.45
limitations: Single centre; reference partly from AI outputs; commercial conflicts; table/abstract inconsistencies
relevance: Rule verifier over LLM extraction; grounding check
supports_or_contradicts: Supports deterministic checking of LLM extraction
claims_supported: Rule-based checking of LLM-extracted facts can remove extraction errors

title: The need for guardrails with large language models in pharmacovigilance and other medical safety critical settings
authors: Joe B. Hakim, Jeffery L. Painter, Darmendra Ramcharran, Vijay Kara, Greg Powell, Paulina Sobczak, Chiho Sato, Andrew Bate, Andrew Beam
published_version_checked: yes - Scientific Reports (via library DOAJ record, earlier pass)
metadata_verified_via: arXiv + library DOAJ record (reused from 2026-11-23 pass)
objective: Guardrails around LLM in pharmacovigilance
architecture_methods: Document anomaly detection, drug/AE term validation against vocabularies, uncertainty communication
main_findings: Abstract reports guardrails eliminate key errors such as incorrect PV terms; no numbers
limitations: Proof of concept; no numbers read
supports_or_contradicts: Supports deterministic guardrails
claims_supported: Rule/vocabulary guardrails proposed for medical safety-critical LLM use

title: EndoGov: A knowledge-governed multi-agent expert system for endometrial cancer risk stratification
authors: Weiye Dai, Liyun Shi, Zanxiang He, Yuling Ma, Mengyuan Lin, Dianxiang Sun, Liming Nie
objective: Guideline-governed multi-agent risk stratification
architecture_methods: Tier-1 specialist agents (deterministic molecular priority rule, rule-based FIGO staging, LLM summaries); Tier-2 governance: deterministic hard-path rules, soft-path deterministic ESMO mapping with LLM chair below confidence threshold, post-hoc deterministic validator; 12 rules in Guideline-KG
models_tools: GPT-4o; Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen2.5-72B swaps; UNI, scGPT
metrics: Accuracy, macro AUC, ECE, guideline violation rate (C-LVR), trigger sensitivity/specificity
baselines: GPT-4o direct; GPT-4o + post-hoc rules; rules only; rules + LogReg; neural multimodal baselines
main_findings: EndoGov acc 0.943, AUC 0.973, C-LVR 0.93%; GPT-4o direct 0.460, C-LVR 17.3%; GPT-4o + rules 0.529, C-LVR 0.0%; rules only 0.800; rules+LogReg 0.884; CPTAC 0.842; validator 26/26 adversarial
limitations: Guideline-derived labels (circularity); rules checked by two researchers; no abstain status; hard/soft rule count inconsistent
relevance: Direct prior art for deterministic decision core + LLM agents; RQ4 rules-only baseline
supports_or_contradicts: Prior art against novelty claim; rules-only beats GPT-4o, challenging LLM premise
claims_supported: Deterministic governance over LLM agents already exists; rules remove violations but do not fix LLM accuracy

title: MedDM: LLM-Executable Clinical Guidance Tree for Clinical Decision-Making
authors: Binbin Li, Xiaoming Shi, Tianxin Meng, Jie Zhai, Tong Ruan
objective: Convert guideline flowcharts into LLM-executable guidance trees
architecture_methods: CV/OCR flowchart extraction; deterministic traversal; LLM answers Yes/No/Unable to determine per node; 'unable' triggers follow-up question
main_findings: 97% mAP (or 98% accuracy) for shape detection; no clinical evaluation
limitations: No decision-quality evaluation; trees may be outdated/erroneous
supports_or_contradicts: Prior art against novelty claim; no evidence of effectiveness
claims_supported: LLM-executable guideline trees with an ask-on-unknown branch predate this project

title: MedGuideX: Internalizing Decision Logic from Executable Guidelines into Large Language Models for Clinical Reasoning
authors: Yuhao Shen, Lang Cao, Simo Du, Yuqing Wang, Juexiao Zhou, Hao Peng, Yue Guo
objective: Train LLMs on executable guideline functions as verifiable rewards
architecture_methods: 841 CPGs -> 2,793 executable Python functions labelling factual/counterfactual QA; SFT + GRPO with execution-matched reward
models_tools: Qwen3.5-4B/9B; GPT-5.0 and others as comparators
metrics: Accuracy; reasoning recall; physician pairwise preference (30 cases)
baselines: RAG, 3-shot, CPGPrompt, CPG fine-tuning, RL with LLM-judged process rewards, frontier and medical LLMs
main_findings: Average 58.77 vs 53.29 base; RAG 54.12; CPGPrompt 40.20; RL-process 56.15; GPT-5.0 65.30
limitations: Small physician study; US-only guidelines; no safety evaluation
supports_or_contradicts: Supports executable guidelines; shows guideline RAG gives small gains
claims_supported: Executable guideline functions can serve as verifiable signals; guideline RAG alone gives limited gains

title: Neuro-Symbolic Resolution of Recommendation Conflicts in Multimorbidity Clinical Guidelines
authors: Shiyao Xie, Jian Du
objective: Detect conflicts/redundancy across guideline recommendations
architecture_methods: LLM agents formalise recommendations into typed predicates/rules (SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm); Z3 SAT/SMT verification
models_tools: DeepSeek-V3.1 + Z3; baselines Qwen-Max, Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-5
main_findings: Conflict F1 0.861 vs GPT-5 0.298 vs DeepSeek-V3.1 0.148; formalisation exact-match 80.1%
limitations: Gold built partly from pipeline output; one drug class; table inconsistencies
supports_or_contradicts: Supports solver-based consistency checks
claims_supported: SMT solvers over LLM-formalised rules far outperform LLMs at detecting guideline conflicts

title: MedRule-KG: A Knowledge-Graph-Steered Scaffold for Mathematical Reasoning with a Lightweight Verifier
authors: Crystal Su
objective: KG + symbolic verifier for drug-drug interaction safety
architecture_methods: Typed KG (CYP, QT); rules C1-C3; post-hoc verifier overrides LLM label
limitations: Circular labels from same rules; tiny; model unnamed
supports_or_contradicts: Weak support; illustrates circular validation risk
claims_supported: Post-hoc symbolic verifiers enforce rules by construction

title: Polaris: A Safety-focused LLM Constellation Architecture for Healthcare
authors: Subhabrata Mukherjee et al. (Hippocratic AI)
objective: Safety-focused multi-agent LLM for patient-facing calls
architecture_methods: Primary LLM + specialist agents (medication, labs, checklist, policy, human intervention); deterministic imperative orchestration; structured outputs parsed by code
dataset_sample: >1,100 nurses and >130 physicians as simulated patients
metrics: Medical safety, clinical readiness, education, conversation quality, bedside manner
main_findings: Developer reports parity with nurses on aggregate; specialists significantly outperform GPT-4 and LLaMA-2 70B (numbers not read)
limitations: Industry self-evaluation; non-diagnostic; numbers not read
supports_or_contradicts: Prior art against novelty claim
claims_supported: Multi-agent LLM with deterministic orchestration and human-escalation agent exists in industry

title: NEURON: A Neuro-symbolic System for Grounded Clinical Explainability
authors: Anuradha Chandrasekaran, Dimitrios Zikos, Mutlu Mete, Alan Pang, Brady D. Lund, Kewei Sha
venue: arXiv 2605.01189v3 (authors state accepted at IEEE CHASE 2026)
published_version_checked: no - IEEE CHASE 2026 proceedings not checked
objective: Neuro-symbolic prediction and grounded explanation
architecture_methods: SNOMED KG embeddings + ontology counts in classical models; RAG LLM narrative from SHAP + deterministic threshold status
models_tools: XGBoost, MLP, AE, SVM; qwen2.5:14b; gpt-oss:20b judge
main_findings: XGBoost AUC 0.73 -> 0.77; LLM still hallucinated drug use
limitations: LLM-judge only; single disease
relevance: KG + LLM; hallucination persists despite grounding
supports_or_contradicts: Supports need for verifier
claims_supported: Grounded LLM explanation still hallucinates without verification

title: Reasoning-Enhanced Healthcare Predictions with Knowledge Graph Community Retrieval
authors: Pengcheng Jiang, Cao Xiao, Minhao Jiang, Parminder Bhatia, Taha Kass-Hout, Jimeng Sun, Jiawei Han
objective: KG community retrieval to enhance LLM clinical predictions
architecture_methods: Multi-source KG, hierarchical community detection and summarisation, dynamic retrieval, LLM reasoning
main_findings: Up to 10.8-15.0% (MIMIC-III) and 12.6-12.7% (MIMIC-IV) improvement
limitations: Abstract only
supports_or_contradicts: Supports KG retrieval
claims_supported: KG community retrieval improves LLM clinical prediction

title: Medi-Gemma: A Hybrid Clinical Decision Support System Integrating Deterministic EMR Analytics and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Mohammed Saim Ahmed Quadri, Yunzhe Xue, Justin W. Ady, Usman Roshan
objective: Hybrid deterministic + RAG CDS for wound care
architecture_methods: Rule-based intent router, ground-truth injection, keyword protocol risk tiers, banned-phrase SafetyVerifier, local Gemma
main_findings: No quantitative results
limitations: No evaluation
supports_or_contradicts: Illustrates unsupported hybrid-safety claims
claims_supported: Hybrid CDS safety claims are often made without evaluation

title: Evaluating the use of large language models to provide clinical recommendations in the Emergency Department
authors: Christopher Y K Williams, Brenda Y Miao, Aaron E Kornblith, Atul J Butte
objective: Evaluate LLM recommendations for admission, radiology, antibiotics in ED
architecture_methods: Zero-shot prompts A-D (incl. caution instruction, CoT)
dataset_sample: UCSF ED notes; 10,000 balanced per task; 200 physician subsample; 1,000 unbalanced
main_findings: Admission accuracy physician 0.83 vs GPT-4-turbo 0.43-0.58; GPT-4-turbo 8% less accurate on average; GPT-3.5 admission sensitivity 1.00, specificity 0.07; 714/1,000 false positives
limitations: Single institution; actual outcomes as ground truth; one resident labeller
supports_or_contradicts: Shows over-caution; supports measuring unnecessary escalation
claims_supported: LLMs are overly cautious in ED recommendations (high sensitivity, low specificity)

title: Triage Performance Across Large Language Models, ChatGPT, and Untrained Doctors in Emergency Medicine: Comparative Study
authors: Lars Masanneck, Linea Schmidt, Antonia Seifert, Tristan Kolsche, Niklas Huntemann, Robin Jansen, Mohammed Mehsin, Michael Bernhard, Sven G Meuth, Lennert Bohm, Marc Pawlitzki
objective: Compare LLM and doctor MTS triage
architecture_methods: Zero-shot triage, 4 queries per model; doctors with GPT-4 second opinion
models_tools: ChatGPT GPT-3.5/GPT-4, GPT-4 API, Llama 3 70B, Gemini 1.5, Mixtral 8x7b
main_findings: Kappa professionals 0.91, untrained doctors 0.68, GPT-4 ChatGPT 0.67, Llama 3 0.52, Mixtral 0.42; LLMs over-triage (Red 12.5-37.1% vs 4% consensus); doctors+GPT-4 0.70 vs 0.68 (P=.97)
limitations: Small single-day sample; zero-shot; over/undertriage numbers in supplement
supports_or_contradicts: Shows over-triage; human+LLM no gain
claims_supported: LLMs over-triage; LLM second opinion did not improve untrained doctors

title: ChatGPT Health performance in a structured test of triage recommendations
authors: Ashwin Ramaswamy et al.
published_version_checked: yes - Nature Medicine (per press release; article not opened)
metadata_verified_via: Institutional press release; reference in Fraile Navarro et al.
objective: Structured test of consumer LLM triage
architecture_methods: 60 scenarios x 16 contextual variations
main_findings: More than half of emergencies under-triaged (51.6% per critique); suicide alerts inverted relative to risk
limitations: Primary paper not read; single time point
supports_or_contradicts: Shows under-triage in consumer setting
claims_supported: Consumer LLM product under-triaged emergencies in structured test

title: Evaluation format, not model capability, drives triage failure in the assessment of consumer health AI
authors: David Fraile Navarro, Farah Magrabi, Enrico Coiera
objective: Test whether forced-choice format drove reported triage failures
architecture_methods: Partial replication; naturalistic vs constrained output; anchoring variants
models_tools: GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro
main_findings: Naturalistic 70.1% vs constrained 63.6% (p=0.015); GPT-5.2 asthma 16% forced-choice vs 100% free text; anchoring dropped Opus 4.6 DKA emergency advice 8/8 to 1/8
limitations: Partial replication; LLM judges; API not product
supports_or_contradicts: Contradicts strong reading of Ramaswamy; warns closed formats can harm escalation
claims_supported: Output format and anchoring change LLM escalation behaviour

title: Reliability of LLMs as medical assistants for the general public: a randomized preregistered study
authors: Andrew M. Bean, Rebecca Elizabeth Payne, Guy Parsons, Hannah Rose Kirk, Juan Ciro, Rafael Mosquera-Gomez, Sara Hincapie M, Aruna S. Ekanayaka, Lionel Tarassenko, Luc Rocher, Adam Mahdi
objective: Test whether lay users benefit from LLMs for condition identification and disposition
architecture_methods: Randomized preregistered user study
main_findings: LLM alone conditions 94.9%, disposition 56.3%; users with LLM conditions <34.5%, disposition <44.2%, no disposition advantage over control; MedQA scores largely uncorrelated with user performance
limitations: Vignettes; older models; lay users not clinicians
relevance: P2 escalation; human factors; P4 benchmark validity
supports_or_contradicts: Shows human-LLM interaction loses LLM performance
claims_supported: Benchmark and LLM-alone performance do not transfer to human-LLM use

title: From Promising Capability to Pervasive Bias: Assessing Large Language Models for Emergency Department Triage
authors: Joseph Lee, Tianqi Shang, Jae Young Baik, Duy Duong-Tran, Shu Yang, Lingyao Li, Li Shen
venue: arXiv 2504.16273v2 (World Scientific open-access chapter; proceedings not identified)

title: Large Language Model Influence on Diagnostic Reasoning: A Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Ethan Goh, Robert Gallo, Jason Hom, Eric Strong, Yingjie Weng, Hannah Kerman, Josephine A. Cool, Zahir Kanjee, Andrew S. Parsons, Neera Ahuja, Eric Horvitz, Daniel Yang, Arnold Milstein, Andrew P.J. Olson, Adam Rodman, Jonathan H. Chen
metadata_verified_via: University of Minnesota experts record + AHRQ PSNet
objective: Effect of LLM access on physician diagnostic reasoning
architecture_methods: Single-blind RCT
metrics: Diagnostic reasoning score; time per case
main_findings: Median 76% vs 74%, difference 2 pp (95% CI -4 to 8; P=.60); LLM alone 16 pp higher than conventional (95% CI 2-30; P=.03); time 519 vs 565 s (ns)
limitations: Vignettes; abstract only
supports_or_contradicts: Physician+LLM no better; LLM alone better
claims_supported: LLM access did not improve physician diagnostic reasoning

title: GPT-4 assistance for improvement of physician performance on patient care tasks: a randomized controlled trial
authors: Ethan Goh et al. (18 authors; last Adam Rodman)
objective: Effect of GPT-4 on physician management reasoning
architecture_methods: Prospective single-blind RCT (NCT06208423)
metrics: Rubric total score; time; harm ratings
main_findings: 43.0% vs 35.7%, diff 6.5% (95% CI 2.7-10.2; P<.001); time 801.5 vs 690.2 s; LLM alone 43.7% vs physicians+LLM 43.0% (ns; sign conflicts in paper); high-harm 4.2% vs 2.9%
limitations: Vignettes; wrong answers not penalised; verbosity confound
supports_or_contradicts: Physician+LLM improved over conventional but not over LLM alone
claims_supported: LLM assistance improves management reasoning modestly; human adds little over LLM alone

title: Automation Bias in Large Language Model Assisted Diagnostic Reasoning Among AI-Trained Physicians
authors: Ihsan Ayyub Qazi, Ayesha Ali, Asad Ullah Khawaja, Muhammad Junaid Akhtar, Ali Zafar Sheikh, Muhammad Hamad Alizai
published_version_checked: no - Sciety links no journal version; NEJM Journal Watch (June 2026) describes a matching trial in NEJM AI, unverified
objective: Measure automation bias from erroneous LLM suggestions
architecture_methods: Single-blind RCT (NCT06963957); deliberate errors in 3 of 6 vignettes
dataset_sample: 44 physicians in Pakistan with 20-h AI training
limitations: Vignettes; artificial errors; 88% of target sample; single session
